These projections was for construction of New Dry Dock at National

The projection was made on the recommendations of Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises (BRPSE) for modernization of shipyard in phases over a period of 3 years.  In
 view thereof, once the revival package of Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Ltd. (HDPEL) is approved, additional funds would be projected at RE stage. Finally, in the case of Inland Waterways Authority of India, an outlay of Rs.358.68 crore was projected for the Annual Plan 2008-09 but the projections have been reduced to Rs.180.00 crore. 10.       The Committee observes that the Department has projected a requirement of Rs.68971.48 crore for the entire 11th Plan.  Against this requirement, the Planning Commission approved an allocation of Rs.67173.40 crore to the Department for carrying out major activities i.e. development of Major Ports, Inland Water Transport, procurement of Dredgers and
 connected activities for the Dredging Corporation of India, Constructions of landing facility  in Andnman and Nicobar Islands, post Tsunami rehabilitation works, Ship Building, Rail Connectivity for the ports and Setusamundrum  Ship Channel Project etc. 
11.       The Committee strongly deplores the tendency of Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance for imposing cuts on the amount demanded by the Department as per their pressing needs.  The Committee feels that if the Department of Shipping has to attain the national growth of 9% in the 11 th Plan period, it will require huge and well planned
 funding.  Thus, the Government spending for the Department of Shipping will have to be significantly stepped up from the present level to meet the growth targets.  The Committee ,therefore, strongly recommends that the Department should be provided with Rs.68971.48 crore by the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance for the 11th Plan period as
 per their original proposal and ensure that no project/scheme proposed by the Department would languish for want of funds.  The Committee also recommends the Department to take appropriate caution and remedial action to absorb in time the allocation made to them.
12.       The Committee wanted to know from the Department of Shipping, the details of shortfall in the expenditure of the Budget Estimates 2007-08, the Department of Shipping informed the Committee that in the Annual Plan 2007-08, an outlay of Rs.4271.27 crore was provided which consists of Gross Budgetary support of Rs.759.00 crore and Internal and
 Extra Budgetary Resources (IEBR) of Rs.3512.27 crore which was revised to Rs.3075.34 crore consisting of Rs. 575.00 crore as Gross Budgetary Support and Rs. 2500.34 crore as IEBR. The anticipated Plan outlay utilisation for the Department of Shipping during 2007-08 is Rs.2517.00 crore
13.       As regards reasons for shortfall in the expenditure of the Budget Estimates 2007-08, the Department of Shipping informed the Committee that :
·
        An outlay of Rs.158.00 crores have been provided for Inland Water Transport out of which Rs.82.60 crores has been released till date.  The shortfall in expenditure is primarily due to delay in sanctioning of project for acquisition of six CSD units for NW-1 and NW-2 and poor response for tenders of dredging, acquisition of vessels, survey and
 navigation equipment. 
·        There is a provision of Rs.40.00 crores in B.E. 2007-08  for meeting the expenditure for Development of Indian Maritime University which has been  reduced to Rs.14.00 crores at RE stage because Expenditure Finance Committee has recommended a cap of Rs.35.00 crores for carrying out preparation work and validation of detailed project report
 for Development of Indian Maritime University.  As Rs.21.00 crores has already been released in the year 2006-07, hence provision of balance amount of Rs.14.00 crore has been kept at RE stage in the year 2007-08.
·        The anticipated plan outlay utilisation for Port Sector during 2007-08 is Rs.1694.71 crore as against the outlay of Rs.2109.76 crore, the saving attributes to various reasons.
·        The subsidy to non-central PSU and private sector shipyards under Non-Plan has been reduced from 132.00 crores to Rs.28.00 crores at the RE stage due to non-materialization of proposals of various companies.
·        In the case of Hindustan Shipyard, there is a provision of Rs.53.18 crores for shipbuilding subsidy which has also been reduced to Rs.44.33 crores at the RE stage as the entire outlay is not likely to be utilized during the period. 
·        The budgetary provision in 2007-2008 for SBR Central Sector Plan Schemes is Rs.6.50 crores out of which Rs.5.50 crores is for R&D Schemes in Shipbuilding and Rs.1.00 crore for Conducting Studies.  So far the Department of Shipping has released Rs.1.00 crore for R&D Schemes in Shipbuilding.  The balance amount of Rs.4.5 crores could not
 be utilized as the Research Committee has not yet approved the proposals.  Rs.0.25 crores has been released for Conducting Studies and another Rs.0.25 crores is expected to be released before the end of the financial year.  The balance amount could not be released as concrete proposals from the organizations were not received.
14.       During the course of the deliberations, the Secretary, Department of Shipping while agreeing to the shortfall deposed before the Committee as under:
“Sir, presently, there have been several difficulties which were highlighted in the earlier discussions with the Committee.  Fortunately, the Model Concession Agreement, which took a long time, is finally in place.  We hope in 2008-09, the roadblocks would be much less because the Model Concession Agreement is in place.  We also intend separating the
 Andamans and Lakshadweep Harbour Works and making them accountable to the local administration.  We would be in a position to submit the progress to the hon. Committee in less than a months’ time.  Better delegation and empowerment at the field level would help us in spending the resources.  We would certainly endeavour to see that we put up a
 better picture next year…….”
15.       The Committee then asked about the plans for utilisation of Rs.6609.00 crore allocated in BE 2008-09, consisting of Gross Budgetary support of Rs.600.00 crore and Internal and Extra Budgetary Resources (IEBR) of Rs.6009.00 crore.  The Department submitted that in so far as Port Sector is concerned, Plan outlay in 2008-09 is Rs. 3650.97 crore
 (comprising 337.98 crore GBS and Rs.3312.99 crore IEBR) as against allocation of Rs. 2109.76 crore in BE 2007-08 (comprising Rs.498.49 crore GBS and Rs.1611.27 crore IEBR).  Increased allocations have been made in Annual Plan 2008-2009 mainly for development of Major Ports, procurement of dredgers and other connected activities of the Dredging
 Corporation of India Ltd. and the Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project.    The utilization of the plan allocation for these schemes/projects will be monitored closely. In the Shipping Sector, an outlay of Rs.25.00 crore was provided in the year 2007-08 for the schemes of Director General of Lighthouses & Lightships which has now been enhanced to Rs.40.00
 crore against projection of Rs.47.00 crore. The enhanced outlay of Rs.15.00 crore will be utilized for establishment of VTS Scheme in Gulf of Kutuch.  Similarly, outlay for IWAI has also been enhanced from Rs.158 crore (2007-08) to Rs.180 crore in 2008-09 to meet the expenditure on the project being executed by IWAI in NW-1, NW-2  and NW-3.  In order
 to ensure optimum utilization of increased allocation, the execution of various schemes/projects will be periodically monitored at higher level.
16.       The Committee is perturbed to note that the Department of Shipping has projected higher plan outlays of Rs.4271.27 crore during the year 2007-08 which was drastically reduced to Rs. 3075.34 crore at RE stage and ultimately, the Department failed to utilize the reduced amount too.  The Department utilized Rs. 2517.00 crore during 2007-08 against the
 budget estimates of Rs.4271.27 crore and surrendered an amount of Rs.1754.27 crore as compared to the BE for the year. The Committee observes that the saving affects almost all the major activities of Department of Shipping be it Inland Water Transport, Shipping, Ports, Lighthouses and Lightships, Shipbuilding etc. and the actual expenditure incurred has
 always been abysmally low compared to the estimated amount. The Committee is not satisfied with the reasons furnished by the Department for non-utilization of the allocations for their being either vague or of routine in nature.   The Committee does not approve the practice being followed by the Department which has been asking for higher allocations year
 after year, but the implementation of projects and schemes were poor as ground realities were not taken into account while formulating and implementing the projects.  The Committee is pained to note that although they have repeatedly recommended for formulation of realistic plans and schemes but no action have been taken by the Government on those
 recommendations.  The Committee expects that intensified monitoring mechanism which is being put in place by the Department, would ensure that budgeted amounts earmarked at the BE stage are fully utilized during 2008-09. At the same time, the Committee recommends that a meaningful and relevant programmes and policies be formulated for regular
 infusion of funds in various projects and schemes in all quarters of the financial year for total utilization of plan outlays  and if required, the Government should review all the on-going schemes periodically for re-allocation of the budgeted amount. The Committee would like to be apprised of the action taken by the Government in this regard.

India with its vast and beautiful coastline, virgin forests and undisturbed idyllic islands, long historical and cultural tradition of architecture, theatre and performing arts can be a fabulous tourist destination. The global scenario for cruise shipping is picking up very fast, with an annual increment from 10-20% in the cruise ship fleet and passengers carried.
 As a departure from the concept of cargo and passenger ships, cruise is like a moving township studded with all state of art facilities including all types of recreational activities. The idea is fast catching because journey on cruise is not only pleasurable, but also comparatively free from sea travel health hazards. Experience in the Caribbean, Latin American and
 South-East Asian countries indicate that huge amount of foreign exchange can be earned by providing the right policy environment and infrastructure for the growth of cruise shipping. With a view to encourage cruise shipping in the country, Government is considering to bring out a comprehensive cruise shipping policy.
53.       The Committee in its 117
th Report on Demands for Grants (2007-08) of the Department of Shipping has dealt with the subject and recommended the Government to formulate a policy for development of cruise shipping in the country.  The Committee enquired the Department about the status of formulation of cruise shipping policy for popularizing cruise
 shipping and development of infrastructure facilities in the country,  the Department of Shipping in their replies submitted that Draft Policy on Cruise Shipping has been under preparation since 28.09.2004 when the High Powered Steering Group under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister (S & RTH) and Co-chaired by Hon’ble Minister of tourism & Culture
 was set up.  As decided in the meeting of High Powered Steering Group, different working Groups were set up to examine issues like immigration, Custom clearance,  Infrastructure at Ports, Taxation, connectivity etc.   Based on the reports of Working Groups, a Draft Cruise Shipping Policy was considered by the High Powered Group in its meeting held on
 6.12.2006.  While there was a consensus about the proposed policy, it was decided that the issue relating to river cruise and environment be also addressed and the matter to include cruise shipping in the LTC be taken up with Ministry of Finance.  Accordingly, a meeting was held on 26 th March, 2007 under the Chairmanship of Secretary (Shipping) to consider
 the issue relating to river cruise and to address environmental matters for inclusion in the draft cruise shipping policy.   The matter was referred to Ministry of Environment and Forests, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Tourism and Director (IWAI) for their comments.   Based on their comments, a Draft Cabinet Note was
 circulated to the concerned Ministries/Departments on 12th September, 2007 for their views.  The views of appraisal agencies have been received, the latest being from Planning Commission on 31.12.2007.  These are under examination.  The comprehensive cruise shipping policy is likely to be finalized in another two months. 
54.       As regards attracting investments from private sector including FDI with a view to develop infrastructure and other facilities for development of cruise  shipping in the country, the Department of Shipping informed that the High Power Steering Group       (HPSG) under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister (SRT&H) with the Union Minister of Tourism
 and Culture as Co-Chairperson was set up to formulate a Cruise Shipping Policy with the objective of making   India a major cruise destination by popularizing Cruise Shipping, facilitating creation of requisite infrastructure and creating a conducive environment.   The Govt. has already allowed 100% FDI in shipping sector including Cruise Shipping. Similarly,
 investment from private sector is also allowed on PPP basis. The draft Cruise Shipping policy provides for development of cruise facilities in the ports in a phased manner. The policy is under finalization in consultation with the concerned Ministries.
55.       The Committee is concerned that despite its recommendations in the earlier reports on Demands for Grants urging the Government to bring out a comprehensive cruise shipping policy, the Government neither complied with its recommendations nor formulated the cruise shipping policy till date although it has been informed by the Department on
 09.01.2008 that the comprehensive cruise shipping policy will be formulated within a period of two months.  The Committee feels that in the absence of a comprehensive cruise shipping policy the Department will not be able to popularize the cruise shipping and address all the aspect of facilitating creation of infrastructure, encourage investments from the
 private sector and create a congenial and hospitable environment for growth of cruise shipping in the country.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates its earlier recommendation urging the Government to bring out a comprehensive policy on cruise shipping without further delay.

76.       Inland waterways comprising of rivers, lakes, canals, creeks, backwaters, etc. extend to about 14,500 kms. in India.  However, the true potential of this important mode of transport is yet to be exploited.
77.       Inland Water Transport (IWT) schemes mainly relate to development of waterways and augmentation of the traffic carrying capacity through expansion and modernization of IWT infrastructure/vessels.   Whereas the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) is responsible for the development of National Waterways, responsibility for the development
 of State Waterways rests with the State Governments. The Central Government has declared three Waterways, viz. Allahabad  – Haldia Stretch (1620 Kms.) Sadiya and Dhubri Stretch (891 kms.) and West Coast Canal from Kollam to Kottapuram stretch along with Udyogamandal Champakara canals (205 kms.) as National Waterways  and are being developed
 by IWAI for shipping and navigation by providing/maintaining basic IWT infrastructure i.e. fairway, navigational aids and terminals.  Three more waterways namely the Kakinada-Puducherry canals along with Godavari and Krishna rivers (1095 km), East Coast Canal along with Brahmani river and Mahanadi  delta (623 km) and Barak river (121 km) are under
 active consideration of the Govt for declaration as new National Waterways.

The Committee feels that worthwhile action should have been taken by the Government on the specific recommendation of the Committee for inclusion of vessels registered under the   Indian Vessels Act, 1917 and the Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 for getting
 tonnage tax benefits for the development of the Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the country.  The Committee apprehends that the Government does not desire to rationalize the fiscal regime for Indian Shipping Industry for facilitating the growth of the Indian tonnage.  The Committee disapproves the contention of
 the Department that introduction of tonnage tax to these vessels would unnecessarily burdened the CIWTC. The Committee desires the Department to conduct a feasibility study to know the profit-loss benefits with the introduction of tonnage tax regime to these vessels and submit a report to the Committee. 
(Para 51)
 
 
CRUISE SHIPPING
            The Committee is concerned that despite its recommendations in the earlier reports on Demands for Grants urging the Government to bring out a comprehensive cruise shipping policy, the Government neither complied with its recommendations nor formulated the cruise shipping policy till date although it has been informed by the
 Department on 09.01.2008 that the comprehensive cruise shipping policy will be formulated within a period of two months.  The Committee feels that in the absence of a comprehensive cruise shipping policy the Department will not be able to popularize the cruise shipping and address all the aspect of facilitating creation of infrastructure,
 encourage investments from the private sector and create a congenial and hospitable environment for growth of cruise shipping in the country.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates its earlier recommendation urging the Government to bring out a comprehensive policy on cruise shipping without further delay. 
(Para 55)
MULTIPLICITY OF TAXES
            The Committee has been drawing attention of the Government to the problem of multiplicity of taxes having adverse impact on shipping sector.  The Government, however, till date has not come out with a proposal for rationalization and as of now there are twelve different taxes ailing the country’s shipping sector particularly the
 EXIM trade.  The Committee feels that Indian shipping will remain uncompetitive unless Government provides the level playing-field as available to other maritime nations in the world.  Since the shipping is truly international business with no commercial barrier, the Committee recommends that the Government must provide a level
 playing field by attempting to rationalize the tax structure and eliminate the disparity in tax treatment which counters the growth of the shipping sector and ultimately tonnage is losing out.  The Committee also recommends the Department to continue to make all out efforts at the highest level till the matter is favourably resolved.  
(Para 58)

(Para 75)
INLAND WATER TRANSPORT
            The Committee has consistently expressed its concern over the slow pace of utilization of plan outlays and development of Inland Water Transport sector in the country. The Committee notes with anguish that an outlay of Rs.158.00 crore was allocated in BE 2007-08 for the IWT sector but it was reduced to Rs.138.60 crore at RE stage
 and an expenditure of Rs.56.53 crore was made only upto February, 2008.   The Committee is disappointed to note the continuous under utilization of funds by the Department of Shipping for development of IWT sector.  The Committee expects that the Department would make every endeavour to ensure that the measures adopted for the
 growth of IWT sector in the country is monitored scrupulously to achieve the envisaged physical and financial targets. 
(Para 81)
            The Committee notes that potential of the  Inland Water Transport remains largely unexplored due to the indifferent attitude of the Central and State Governments. The Committee observes that although the Department of Shipping is committed to increase the share of Inland Water Transport in the country’s total EXIM trade, still
 the waterways are not being utilized to their potential and remain largely neglected and underdeveloped for want of required infrastructure namely fairways, terminals and navigable aids, as a result, it has not reached at a threshold level to become commercially viable. The Committee is of the view that with adequate investments, policy
 framework and focused approach, the Inland Water Transport in the country can be developed into a viable transport mode complementary to the rail and road modes. The Committee is of the opinion that to develop the Inland Water Transport sector with fast pace to its full potential in the country, the Government should endeavor to
 provide institutional framework and minimize the procedural bottlenecks besides providing adequate investments both from public and private partnership primarily public investment in Inland Water Transport and to develop it to a level where private sector feels confident to invest in this sector particularly in ownership and operation of
 cargo and passenger vessels to Inland Water Transport mode. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Government to provide institutional framework and basic infrastructural facility for accelerated development of Inland Water Transport sector in the country under National Maritime Development Programme.
(Para 82)
            The Committee notes with dismay over the discontinuance of the centrally sponsored scheme for IWT development in the country by the Planning Commission.  The Committee is of the view that the decision of the Planning Commission to convert the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for IWT development into central sector
 scheme will adversely affect the pace of development of Inland Water Transport in the country.  The Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to impress upon the Planning Commission for the revival of the central sponsored scheme for overall development of the IWT Sector during the annual plan itself.
(Para 93)
            The Committee is constrained to note that cargo transportation by Inland Water Transport mode has not shown significant improvement on the three National Waterways.  The Committee also expresses its displeasure over the fact that no comparative cost-output evaluation for transportation of cargo through this inland water
 transport has been carried out by the Department.  The Committee is of the view that such evaluation would further establish the support of Inland Water Transport over other mode of transports.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that a detailed study should be carried out by the Department in this regard. The Committee also urges
 the Department to fix realistic physical target for cargo transportation by IWT mode year-wise for entire 11
th Plan period and put in place institutional monitoring mechanism for achieving the desired growth.
(Para 94)
CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION
            The Committee notes with anguish that no security personnel are being provided for safe transportation of men and material in Suderbans/Protocol routes in West Bengal.   The Committee is of the opinion that security is a prime concern and should be looked into seriously by making commensurate security arrangement in
 Suderbans/Protocol routes.  The Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to take up the matter of beefing-up of security arrangement in the Suderbans/Protocol routes with the Union Home Ministry so that inadequacy of police deployment could be addressed in a big way.
(Para 97)
            The Committee is pained to note that the Government has decided neither to consider revival of CIWTC nor to amalgamate this Corporation with various Organizations, such as Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) that too, without getting conducted any
 scientific study by an expert agency.  The Committee is of the view that the matter of revival and amalgamation of CIWTC should be got examined by some high powered expert committee.    The Committee once again reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in 117 th Report on Demands for Grants 2007-08 of Department of
 Shipping, which is reproduced below:
“The Committee is constrained to note that inspite of its recommendation in the past, the Government has not come out with a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing assets of River Service Division (RSD). The Committee is of the opinion that CIWTC with its infrastructure and expertise can play an integral part
 for development and promotion of inland water transport through NW-I and NW-II. The Committee recommends that possibility may also be explored to physically amalgamate the remaining CIWTC with Inland Water Transport Authority of India (IWAI) or Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India
 (SCI), so that the infrastructure and expertise of CIWTC can be utilized for development of waterways transport.”
(Para 100)
DEVELOPMENT OF WATER TRANSPORT IN ANDAMAN & NICOBAR AND LAKSHADWEEP ISLANDS
            The Shipping Corporation of India with its two owned passenger-cum-cargo vessels and 27 managed vessels operates domestic passenger-cum-transportation services between mainland and Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshdweep group of islands on behalf of the Government of India.  Presently, Andaman and Nicobar Island
 administration has 22 vessels comprising of 18 passenger vessels and 4 passenger-cum-cargo vessels, Union Territory of Lakshdweep has 5 vessels comprising 1 passenger-cum-cargo vessel, 3 passenger vessels and one bunker barge.  The Committee observes that water transport is the life-line of these groups of islands for their
 interconnection with the mainland and within islands.  The Committee notes that this sector has been neglected for so many years without any fund infusion for modernization of the vessels and purchase of additional vessels.  Due to this, the populations of these islands are suffering to a great extent.  The Committee further notes that in the
 Demand-for-Grants for the year 2008-09 no financial allocation has been made for improving the interconnectivity and water transport in Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshdweep islands.  The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Government of India to take immediate steps for improving inter-islands connectivity of the
 islands of Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshdweep for mitigating the problems of connectivity between these islands.  The Committee also recommends that sufficient Budgetary Allocation may be provided for augmenting the water transport connectivity in these islands.
(Para 101)
